titleEn: While We Grind, Draw in Flour!

pages.text: "Dad, is it done?" Little brother Mumu shuffled beside Dad at the mill. The millstones rattled, turning wheat to flour a little at a time. They would bake bread with it tonight. Mumu wanted to eat soon.
"A whole sack takes a while." Dad poured another handful into the millstones. Snow fell heavily outside, and the wheel turned slowly. "When will it be done...?" Mumu pouted his beak.
"Bored! Why are the stones so slow?" Leaning on a wheat sack, Mumu twisted his body. Still rattle, rattle. Big sister Dodo sat on a sack, swinging her legs.
Dad winked. "Look at the floor, Mumu. White flour everywhere, right? Shall we draw there? While we grind, draw in flour!" "What's drawing in flour?" Mumu tilted his head.
"Stamp a webbed foot." Mumu stamped the floor. Tap, tap, tap! Duck footprints gathered in a circle on white flour. "Wow! A flower!" His eyes sparkled.
Now Dodo's turn. With her long wingtip, she swept through the flour. "A waterwheel!" The boring floor filled with pictures.
"A snowman!" Mumu drew. "Dad's straw hat!" Dodo drew. Taking turns, they called together, "While we grind, draw in flour!" Dad smiled as he poured wheat into the stones.
"Look how much flour!" Mumu peered into the sack below. More flour piled up than before. Excited, he flicked his tail.
Mumu turned to Dodo and raised both wings. "One, stamp flowers with duck feet! Two, draw with wingtips! Three, take turns with my sister!" "Next time we wait, let's do it again!" Dodo nodded.

A sack full of white flour! Under his straw-hat brim, Dad gave Mumu a snug hug. "Turn boring time into play, and it passes quickly, right? Bread tonight!" Stamping his foot, Mumu called, "While we grind, draw in flour!"
